title: VIP Month 1 Week 3: Theory of Consumer Behaviour

questions.text: If MU of coffee = 30 and P<sub>coffee</sub> = 10, while MU of bread = 20 and P<sub>bread</sub> = 5, what should the consumer do?
options: A) Buy more coffee, less bread
B) Buy more bread, less coffee
C) Buy equal amounts of both
questions.correct_answer: B) Buy more bread, less coffee
questions.explanation: Compare MU/P: Coffee = 30/10 = 3 utils/Birr. Bread = 20/5 = 4 utils/Birr. Bread gives MORE utility per Birr (4 > 3), so buy MORE bread.

questions.text: If TU = 10Q - Q², what is the MU when Q = 3?
At consumer equilibrium, which condition holds?
questions.explanation: Consumer equilibrium requires equal MU per Birr for ALL goods.

questions.text: If consumer income doubles and prices also double, the budget line:
questions.explanation: If income and prices BOTH double, purchasing power is unchanged (2M/2P = M/P).

questions.text: If MRS = 2, the consumer is willing to give up:
options: A) 2 units of Y for 1 unit of X
B) 1 unit of Y for 2 units of X
C) 2 units of X for 1 unit of Y
questions.correct_answer: A) 2 units of Y for 1 unit of X
questions.explanation: MRS = 2 means give up 2 units of Y for 1 more unit of X.

questions.text: Which violates the assumptions of consumer preferences?
options: A) A > B and B > C implies A > C
B) Consumer prefers A over B and B over A simultaneously
C) Consumer is indifferent between A and B
D) Consumer prefers more to less
questions.correct_answer: B) Consumer prefers A over B and B over A simultaneously
questions.explanation: This violates COMPLETENESS — cannot prefer A over B AND B over A at same time.

questions.text: If MU is NEGATIVE, Total Utility is:
questions.explanation: Negative MU means each additional unit REDUCES total satisfaction.

questions.text: An indifference curve is CONVEX to the origin because of:
questions.explanation: Diminishing MRS creates convex shape — willing to give up less and less Y for each X.

questions.text: If Px = 5, Py = 10, and Income = 100, what is the slope of the budget line?
The ordinal utility approach uses which tool for analysis?
options: B) Indifference curves and budget lines
questions.correct_answer: B) Indifference curves and budget lines
questions.explanation: Ordinal utility uses IC + Budget lines for consumer equilibrium.

questions.text: If TU from 5 units = 100 and TU from 6 units = 105, what is MU of the 6th unit?
A price increase of Good X causes the budget line to:
questions.explanation: Price increase reduces max X, pivoting line inward on X-axis.

questions.text: Which point is CONSUMER EQUILIBRIUM?
options: A) Where IC is below budget line
B) Where IC is tangent to budget line
C) Where IC intersects budget line twice
questions.correct_answer: B) Where IC is tangent to budget line
questions.explanation: Equilibrium = highest IC tangent to budget line (MRS = Px/Py).

questions.text: If MUx = 40, Px = 8, MUy = 30, Py = 6, what should the consumer do?
questions.explanation: MUx/Px = 40/8 = 5. MUy/Py = 30/6 = 5. Already at equilibrium!

questions.text: A Giffen good violates the Law of Demand because:
options: A) Demand increases when price increases
B) Demand decreases when price increases
C) Supply increases when price increases
questions.correct_answer: A) Demand increases when price increases
questions.explanation: Giffen goods have upward-sloping demand due to income effect overwhelming substitution effect.

questions.text: If Income = 200, Px = 20, Py = 10, what are the intercepts?
questions.explanation: X-intercept = 200/20 = 10. Y-intercept = 200/10 = 20.

questions.text: The assumption of transitivity is important because it ensures:
options: B) Preferences are consistent and logical
questions.correct_answer: B) Preferences are consistent and logical
questions.explanation: Transitivity ensures logical, consistent preferences.

questions.text: In cardinal utility, if MU > Price, the consumer should:
options: A) Buy MORE of the good
B) Buy LESS of the good
questions.correct_answer: A) Buy MORE of the good
questions.explanation: If MU > Price, satisfaction exceeds cost — buy more until MU = Price.

questions.text: Indifference curves for PERFECT SUBSTITUTES are:
questions.explanation: Perfect substitutes have constant MRS → straight line ICs.

questions.text: If MU is constant (not diminishing), the TU curve is:
questions.explanation: Constant MU means TU increases linearly (straight line).
